subject: Unexpected bill jump — possible 'heartbeat' double-counting
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@atlasops.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden April 17 usage spike — can you help?

Hi Aisha,

Hope you're well. We noticed a ~6x jump in token consumption on 2028-04-17 (see attached CSV snapshot) that doesn't line up with any product release or spike in user traffic on our side. The majority of calls show very short outputs but are counted as full-response token usage.

I checked client-side and didn't see repeated user requests; our infra team suspects a keepalive/heartbeat pattern introduced in a background worker that talks to your streaming endpoint. Could that be counted twice on your side (client + server echoes) or otherwise double-counted?

We put the account on an invoice hold while we investigate — open to a quick triage call. Attaching the usage snapshot and a short sampling of responses.

Attachments: atlasops-usage-snapshot-20280417.csv

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
VP Engineering, AtlasOps
samir@atlasops.com
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@atlasops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden April 17 usage spike — can you help?

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the CSV.

On Tue, Apr 18, 2028 at 9:12 AM Samir Patel <samir@atlasops.com> wrote:
> We noticed a ~6x jump in token consumption on 2028-04-17...

Ben (billing) and Marissa (finance) are looped in to help with credits and any invoice hold. Ben — can your team pull a short telemetry slice for AtlasOps for 2028-04-17 and confirm whether we see duplicate request IDs or unusually high prefix counts from streaming sessions? If we identify an overcount, we'll propose a provisional credit while we trace the root cause.

Samir — can you also share a 5–10 line sample (raw request/response headers and timestamps) from a suspect session and indicate any client-side retries or keepalive period you use? That will speed root cause triage.

I'll set up an internal ticket and follow up today.

Cheers,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@atlasops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden April 17 usage spike — telemetry slice requested

Hi Aisha / Samir,

Thanks for the context. I pulled a quick telemetry slice for AtlasOps between 2028-04-17T00:00Z and 2028-04-17T23:59Z. Initial findings:
- 78% of the additional token volume is associated with streaming endpoints (route: /v1/streams/generate)
- We see a cluster of sessions where the same session_id appears in very short windows (sub-10s gaps) with tiny response payloads (~1–3 tokens)
- For those sessions, the request_id header is sometimes unique per TCP connection but the x-session-id (client session) is repeated — suggests client retried keepalive pings or the client sent heartbeat frames that our meter currently treats as separate responses

Samir — if you can attach the sample lines you mentioned, please redact any PII. From our side, the next steps are:
1) Engineering to determine whether we are counting heartbeats as billable token events (short-term fix: dedupe events with identical session_id and identical prompt hash inside a 15s window)
2) If we confirm overcounting, offer a provisional credit for the delta while we implement the dedupe rule and reprocess the day's usage for AtlasOps

Marissa, please standby for a provisional credit estimate once engineering confirms the delta.

Ben Carter
Senior Billing Operations Manager
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Samir Patel <samir@atlasops.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Apr 2028 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden April 17 usage spike — telemetry slice requested

Thanks Ben — attaching the short sample export (redacted). Two sample sessions below (excerpt):

-- sample-session-1 --
2028-04-17T14:02:03.123Z session_id=svc-42abc prompt_hash=0x7f2f req_id=rcv-9a1 conn_id=socket-12 type=heartbeat
2028-04-17T14:02:03.221Z session_id=svc-42abc prompt_hash=0x7f2f req_id=rcv-9a2 conn_id=socket-12 type=response tokens_in=2 tokens_out=0
2028-04-17T14:02:03.400Z session_id=svc-42abc prompt_hash=0x7f2f req_id=rcv-9a3 conn_id=socket-12 type=response tokens_in=0 tokens_out=1

-- sample-session-2 --
2028-04-17T16:21:11.001Z session_id=svc-90f1 prompt_hash=0x1ad4 req_id=rcv-7b4 conn_id=socket-99 type=heartbeat
2028-04-17T16:21:11.109Z session_id=svc-90f1 prompt_hash=0x1ad4 req_id=rcv-7b5 conn_id=socket-99 type=response tokens_in=3 tokens_out=2
2028-04-17T16:21:11.209Z session_id=svc-90f1 prompt_hash=0x1ad4 req_id=rcv-7b6 conn_id=socket-99 type=response tokens_in=0 tokens_out=1

Notes: our client opens a persistent socket and sends a lightweight heartbeat frame every ~100ms when idle; when the server sends any data back it may generate a new internal req_id for bookkeeping. We didn't expect heartbeats to be billable.

Attachments: atlasops-usage-snapshot-20280417.csv

Let us know what you find. Happy to give you a short window to reprocess if that will resolve the invoice.

—Samir
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@atlasops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Apr 2028 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden April 17 usage spike — proposed resolution

Samir — quick update and proposed next steps after internal review: we confirmed that our current streaming meter increments token counts on any short response frames and does not dedupe heartbeats or identical prompt hashes inside ephemeral sessions. Your samples match the pattern we saw in telemetry (same session_id, multiple tiny responses within <1s).

What we'll do:
- Short-term (within 48 hours): engineering will run a reprocess for 2028-04-17 for AtlasOps applying a dedupe rule: ignore response frames marked as heartbeat or drop additional response events for the same session_id + prompt_hash within a 15-second window. This should remove the bulk of the extra token counts.
- Credit: pending exact delta from reprocess, we will provisionally apply a credit equal to the identified overage (expected ~72% of the spike per Ben's slice). We will not invoice while the reprocess is underway.
- Medium-term: engineering will add an explicit heartbeat flag on our streaming API and update docs; we'll also verify SDK behavior so keepalives are not billed.

Ben / Marissa — please prepare a provisional credit entry for AtlasOps (estimate: credit = $18,400) and hold invoice until we close the reprocess. Marissa — attach the provisional credit note to DEAL-4812 in HubSpot (link above).

Samir — thanks for the sample — that made triage fast. Once reprocess completes I'll share the final reconciliation and the credit memo. If it's urgent, we can schedule a 20-minute call to walk through the telemetry in real time.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
